result.instructions: sqzrlite: index-only code navigation for AI agents. Exact search, structural map and symbol navigation over a local index; no embeddings, no vector store, no external services.

tools.name: symbol_lookup
tools.title: Look up symbol
tools.description: Look up an exact symbol by name across the indexed workspace: signature, doc comment, file:span, and body within the token budget (maxTokens, default 300) — the method you named, not the whole file. When a type's body does not fit the budget, the hit carries its member list (name, kind, line) plus membersOmitted instead, so the next call is expand_span on the member you want. Not-found returns an empty result, not an error; expand_span widens the context around a hit. Pass the symbol as 'name' or its alias 'symbol' — both are accepted, a wrong-param error names both.

tools.name: expand_span
tools.title: Expand span
tools.description: Read the exact lines you need from the live file on disk: the span plus contextLines of surrounding context, around coordinates from code_search/symbol_lookup — reflects edits made after indexing, and is the only tool that returns raw source lines. When truncated is true, context (before/after) may be partially filled — the span itself has priority.

tools.name: find_references
tools.title: Find references
tools.description: Callers of a symbol before you edit it: every reference as file:line with the reference kind and the enclosing symbol, name-exact with no false positives (unlike grep on a name), one row per callsite even when several same-name definitions share the reference set. Every row names its repo, so callsites that only look identical across repositories stay distinct; the envelope also carries definitions ({repo, kind, file, startLine, endLine}) naming the declarations behind the rows: whenever two or more same-name declarations share one callsite list, or nothing calls the symbol at all. A row set belongs to the declaring file's last parse: a caller indexed after a declaring file's newest parse can leave this stale — the declaring files appear in warnings with the lag named, and 'sqzrlite index' reconciles every caller now. Returns a tool error if the symbol is not indexed. Pass the symbol as 'symbol' or its alias 'name' — both are accepted, a wrong-param error names both. Pair with symbol_lookup to jump from a match to its usages.

tools.name: index_status
tools.title: Index status
tools.description: Workspace freshness and coverage, index-only: per-repo file/symbol/chunk counts, per-kind chunk counts (data.kindChunks maps "code" and "docs" to chunk totals; the values sum to the per-repo chunks counts), index age, and the resolved workspace rootPath — if rootPath is not your project's root, this session serves a different workspace. data.semantic reads "unsupported": this lite server carries no embeddings and no vector store, so the full product's embeddings/qdrant blocks are absent rather than zeroed. When more than one workspace is registered, data.workspaces also lists them as {name, rootPath, storeKey, current, stale} (up to 12 rows, the rest counted in workspacesOmitted) — an absent workspaces key means this session's workspace is the only one the registry knows.

tools.name: code_search
tools.title: Search code
tools.description: Exact search over the indexed workspace: matches exact identifiers and domain-worded phrase fragments ("VectorDimensionMismatchException" or "validate config file") against the trigram index. Returns file:line matches with snippets, never full bodies — expand_span reveals a body around a hit. One hit per file: the best span wins and the file's other spans collapse into alsoMatched, so topK counts distinct files, not spans. Pass prefix (e.g. "src/") to scope the search to one directory subtree. kind filters what a hit can be: "all" (default) matches everything, "code" keeps program sources, "docs" keeps prose and config (markdown, text, json, yaml, toml, xml). This lite server has no semantic arm: paraphrase-matching is unavailable and answers come from the exact arms only.

tools.name: code_pack
tools.title: Code pack
tools.description: Answer "what is this symbol and who touches it" in ONE call: definition (signature, doc comment, file:span), the defining member's body within the budget (maxTokens default 2000), every caller as file:line rows, and per-file cost — instead of chaining symbol_lookup → expand_span → find_references. Budget order: definition and body spend first, callers truncate (the withheld count is in the response). complete:false names the way out; expand_span reads the exact lines around any coordinate. Per-tool exactness stays available: symbol_lookup, find_references and expand_span keep their contracts.

tools.name: repo_map
tools.title: Repository map
tools.description: Structural map of the indexed repositories: nested directory/file tree rendered as indented lines with type/member signatures (depth 1 = dirs, 2 = files, 3 = members), never bodies. The cheapest first contact with an unfamiliar workspace — orient across repos, dirs and entry points before reading any file. Pass prefix (e.g. "src/Squeezr.Cli/") to render only that subtree with prefix-relative directory labels — depth keeps its structural meaning. Lines come from the index: one structural pass over the indexed rows reports files missing from disk or changed by size or mtime in staleFiles — a bounded sample of what it found, never the full verdict, with the covered row count and the sample size stated in warnings. Nothing is reindexed on this call; expand_span reads code on coordinates from other tools.
